heading: What `logical: false` is not
text:
### What `logical: false` is not [LNOG.1.3]

- Not a synonym for `realtime`.  `realtime` does not imply `logical: false`.  TMS
  under `realtime` is pre-sized and rt_locked, making it bounded hard-RT.
  `logical: false` is an optional further constraint that eliminates the
  TMS entirely.
- Not a performance dial.  It is a semantic constraint.  A
  `logical: false` program has fundamentally different fact lifecycle
  behaviour from a program with logical facts.
- Not equivalent to writing all rules with `emit X` (explicit lifecycle)
  instead of `emit X logical`.  The difference is that `logical: false`
  also eliminates the TMS data structure from the runtime, whereas a
  program that happens not to use `logical` but keeps `logical: true` still allocates and
  initialises the TMS.
